The '''2018–19 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team''' represented [[Indiana University (Bloomington)|Indiana University]] in the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Archie Miller (basketball)|Archie Miller]], in his second year as Indiana head coach. The team played its home games at [[Assembly Hall (Bloomington)|Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall]] in [[Bloomington, Indiana]], as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The season officially kicked off with its annual event, Hoosier Hysteria, on September 29, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2018/07/17/indiana-sets-hoosier-hysteria-for-saturday-september-29/|title=Indiana sets Hoosier Hysteria for Saturday, September 29 |work=Inside the Hall|access-date=2018-07-17|language=en}}</ref>

Despite getting off to a strong start of 12–2, which included three conference wins, IU struggled mightily down the backstretch of the season. Riddled with injuries and the inability to shoot, the Hoosiers lost 12 of 13 games before turning things around and finishing the regular season with a four-game winning streak. Having put themselves back into the conversation for making the NCAA Tournament for the first time in three years, the Hoosiers looked to knock off [[2018–19 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in the [[2019 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]]. With a win, many bracketologists had IU safely in the field. However, the Hoosiers fell short and lost to Ohio State, 79–75. IU was deemed one of the Last Four Out in the NCAA Tournament, so they earned 1-seed in the [[2019 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]], where they advanced to the quarterfinals before losing to [[2018–19 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]], 73–63. Thus, the Hoosiers' 119th season ended with an overall record of 19–16 and 8–12 in the Big Ten.

==Previous season==
Miller's first season was a major remodeling job, starting with laying the foundation of a pack-line defense and valuing possessions. Early in the season, Miller stated practices were 75% defense, 25% offense.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/indiana/Article/Transcript-Archie-Miller-at-IU-media-day-108128981/|title=Transcript: Archie Miller at IU media day|website=Peegs.com}}</ref> That scheme showed early and often, as the Hoosiers struggled mightily throughout the season to find any flow or rhythm on offense, despite the defense making leaps and bounds in the overall rankings of Division 1 basketball.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2018/04/10/thats-a-wrap-team-defense-6/|title=That's A Wrap: Team defense|date=10 April 2018}}</ref> With a surprising early second round loss in the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|2018 Big Ten tournament]] to [[2017–18 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]], 76–67, and losing enough games to keep them out of both the NCAA tournament and NIT, including games in which they were favored, such as [[2017–18 Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball team|Indiana State]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2017/11/10/16636112/indiana-state-hoosiers-archie-miller-embarrassment-blowout|title=Indiana State embarrasses Indiana in Archie Miller's debut|first=Mike|last=Rutherford|date=10 November 2017|website=SBNation.com}}</ref> and [[2017–18 Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball team|Fort Wayne]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news-sentinel.com/news/local-news/2017/12/18/fort-wayne-mastodons-knock-off-iu-again/|title=Fort Wayne Mastodons knock off IU…again}}</ref> IU's first season under their new coach came to a disappointing close. They finished with an overall record of 16–15 and 9–9 in the Big Ten.

==Offseason==

===Departures===
On April 12, 2018, junior forward [[Juwan Morgan]] announced he was entering the [[2018 NBA draft|NBA draft]], but he would not sign with an agent.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2018/04/12/iu-basketballs-juwan-morgan-declares-draft-wont-hire-agent/511299002/|title=IU basketball's Juwan Morgan declares for draft, won't hire agent|work=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2018-04-13|language=en}}</ref> However, on May 29, 2018, it was revealed that he had withdrawn from the draft and would return for his senior season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2018/05/29/juwan-morgan-returning-to-indiana-for-senior-season/|title=Juwan Morgan returning to Indiana for senior season|work=Inside the Hall|access-date=2018-05-29|language=en}}</ref>

===Recruiting class===
With the commitment of [[Romeo Langford]] on April 30, 2018, not only did Archie Miller recruit his first 5-star player, he also landed IU's first [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] since [[Cody Zeller]] in 2011. He also signed two other finalists for the award, [[Rob Phinisee]] and Damezi Anderson. Miller rounded out the incoming class with the second best player from Ohio in Jerome Hunter, as well as another 4-star, Jake Forrester from Pennsylvania; this group of high school seniors comprised a Top 10 2018 recruiting class. Within the state of Indiana, there was a total of four 5- and 4-star 2018 recruits, three of whom committed to Indiana. The last addition to the team roster was made on May 3, 2018, when graduate transfer Evan Fitzner of [[Saint Mary's College of California|Saint Mary's College]] claimed the final scholarship available.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2018/05/03/st-marys-graduate-transfer-evan-fitnzer-commits-to-indiana/|title=St. Mary's graduate transfer Evan Fitzner commits to Indiana|publisher=Inside the Hall|last=Bozich|first=Alex|date=May 3, 2018|access-date=May 3, 2018}}</ref>

==Schedule and results==
The 2018–19 season marked the first time in [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] history that the teams played a 20-game conference schedule.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/big-ten-adds-two-games-for-a-20-game-conference-schedule-starting-in-2018-19/|title=Big Ten adds two games for a 20-game conference schedule starting in 2018–19|work=CBS Sports|date=October 19, 2017|access-date= March 9, 2018|last=Norlander|first=Matt}}</ref> The new schedule also included a regional component to increase the frequency of games among teams in similar areas. Over the course of a six-year cycle (12 playing opportunities), in-state rivals play each other 12 times, regional opponents play 10 times, and all other teams play nine times.<ref name=":0" /> Three in-state series are guaranteed home-and-homes; Illinois and Northwestern, Indiana and Purdue, and Michigan and Michigan State will always play twice.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21076233/big-ten-play-20-game-conference-schedule-next-season|title=Big Ten to move to 20-game conference slate|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-03-12}}</ref>
